Non-Manifold Repair

`init_file/scene.blend` contains a single mesh object `Part` with geometric defects — missing faces and duplicate/loose vertices. Repair the mesh so it is closed-manifold while preserving the object's overall shape, and save the result to `output/repaired.blend` (relative to the working directory).

## Pass conditions
1. `output/repaired.blend` opens as a valid Blender file containing exactly one mesh object, named `Part`.
2. `Part.location` matches the input's value to within 1e-5 per axis.
3. No edge of `Part` is non-manifold — every edge is shared by exactly two faces.
4. `Part` has no loose vertices (every vertex is incident to at least one edge).
5. `Part` has no loose edges (every edge bounds at least one face).
6. `Part`'s signed volume is positive, i.e. face normals are outward-consistent.
7. The axis-aligned bounding box of `Part`'s vertex coordinates matches the input's bbox to within 1% relative difference per axis.
8. `Part`'s unsigned volume differs from its AABB volume by less than 2% (the shape fully fills its bounding box).

Do not remesh, decimate, or rescale — the repair should touch only the defective regions.
source: Blender Manual — Mesh Analysis and Cleanup (Make Manifold)
